newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says talks with U.S. stuck over 'open skies'.
newsitem.headline: Japan says talks with U.S. stuck over 'open skies'.

text.p: The question of whether "open skies" should be the principle behind air deregulation remains a huge sticking point in air talks between the United States and Japan, a Japanese Transport Ministry official said on Wednesday.
The official also told reporters that the United States has asked that claims by cargo carrier Federal Express Corp be given priority in the talks.
But Japan has said that passenger and cargo issues should not be separated, he added.
Federal Express is seeking an expansion of its "beyond rights" -- the right to fly on to a third country -- in particular to China.
The two countries have completed the first of two to three days of aviation talks in Portland, Oregon, in their latest effort to set the stage for a more liberal accord.

Washington wants Japan to agree that open skies -- the lifting of all government restrictions except for safety and security rules -- should be their final goal, although it is willing to accept a phased approach to deregulation.
But Tokyo, while saying it favours deregulation, argues that open skies only led to U.S.-dominated alliances that stifle competition.
Japanese negotiators are willing to be "more flexible" in their proposals if Washington drops its insistence on open skies, the official said.
